FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Places in the Community flashcards.

Twenty-eight places a child’s town is made of, on twenty-eight cards a kid can read. Each card names one place — the library with its open book, the fire station with its truck asleep between the doors, the bakery that smells like tomorrow’s breakfast — and each card page carries a simple guide: who works there, what we do there, and the words to say when we arrive. The town speaks the everyday words of the US, UK and Canada — and where the countries differ (movie theater and cinema, drugstore and chemist’s, gas station and petrol station), both names ride along, so every family hears its own hometown talking.

Every card in the set.

Each card has its own page, and every card shows its age pill — start with the group that fits your child today.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    The Town Walk draw

    Stack the cards face down, draw one, place it at the end of a growing street on the floor, and say what you do there — "at the bakery, I buy bread!" Walk the whole town when the street is finished.

  2. 02

    Same place, two names

    The cards quietly carry both flavors of English: movie theater and cinema, drugstore and chemist’s, gas station and petrol station, shopping cart and trolley. Say both — your child picks a favorite, or keeps both like secrets.

  3. 03

    Before-we-go practice

    Going somewhere today? Pull that card out and talk it through first — the dentist lesson before the check-up, the bus-stop lesson before the first ride. The visit feels half-familiar before you arrive.

  4. 04

    Who works here?

    Lay out four place cards and match the helper to the building: the doctor at the hospital, the librarian at the library, the baker at the bakery, the officer at the police station. Every place has its people.

  5. 05

    The errand map

    Arrange three or four cards in the order of a real errand day — bank, post office, supermarket — and follow the map together, out loud, at home or in the car.
